description: NASA Space Apps Challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten" meydan okuması için hazır ekibimizle yer alıyoruz! Amacımız; Three.js ve modern web teknolojileriyle, kullanıcıların Ay ve Mars yüzeyinde gezinebileceği, terk edilmiş roket kademelerini ve araçları keşfedeceği 3D dijital deneyim inşa etmektir. Tarih, bilim ve yazılımı harmanlayarak uzay keşiflerinin mirasını geleceğe aktarıyoruz.
summary:
Project Yigido Orbit: "Abandoned in Space" is an open-access, zero-install 3D digital museum, educational archive, and space archaeology atlas running seamlessly across standard desktop, tablet, and mobile browsers. It catalogs humanity's historical space hardware left across the Moon, Mars, Venus, and the Outer Solar System, reframing discarded spacecraft not as space debris, but as interplanetary cultural heritage under the Artemis Accords and NASA SP-2024-4559.

Developed with pure JavaScript and Three.js procedural WebGL, the platform integrates NASA PDS coordinates, real-time Mars weather telemetry, and verified LROC/HiRISE archival photography across seven decades of exploration. Users can explore 3D orbital globes, inspect interactive CAD wireframe models, listen to restored radio transmissions, and experience authentic descent physics. To elevate spatial understanding, the platform includes an optional 1:1 scale WebXR exploration tool, allowing users to perceive the true human scale of these historic machines without requiring specialized hardware for the core museum experience.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

"Project Yigido Orbit: Abandoned in Space" is a universally accessible, browser-first educational platform and 3D digital atlas that preserves the material record of humanity's lunar and planetary missions. Users can navigate 3D globes of the Moon, Mars, Venus, and Titan directly in any modern web browser (desktop, tablet, or mobile). The platform features an interactive timeline spanning from the 1960s to the 2020s, a 5-Act guided historical narrative tour, authentic 3D PBR/wireframe CAD inspection viewports, restored Quindar audio transmissions, and real-time Mars telemetry (Sol clock, temperature, atmospheric pressure). To maximize interactivity and spatial learning, the platform also offers an optional 1:1 scale astronaut perspective tool (accessible via desktop WASD or WebXR-enabled devices like Meta Quest), allowing users to step beside landers and inspect their human proportions.

What benefits and intended impact does it have?

As humanity returns to deep space through the Artemis program, historical planetary landing sites face threats from rocket plume sandblasting and human interference. Our platform establishes an open-access space archaeology baseline for educators, researchers, and students worldwide. By presenting these artifacts through human stories, engineering trade-offs (e.g., why equipment was discarded to save liftoff mass), and long-term space weathering data, we turn dry orbital numbers into an engaging science communication bridge.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

• Languages & Standards: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), WebGL, Web Audio API, WebXR Device API, Gamepad API.

• Core 3D Engine: Three.js (r128) with 100% procedural code generation and runtime canvas textures. Zero external 3D modeling dependencies (no Blender, no bulky GLTF downloads), enabling instantaneous sub-2-second page loads on any device.

• Multi-Platform Optimization: Responsive touch controls for mobile/tablet users, mouse/keyboard for desktops, and dual-mode controller support for Meta Quest Browser.

How is your project creative?

We combine rigorous orbital mechanics with emotional human storytelling. Each artifact details the human rationale behind abandonment, long-term vacuum preservation states, and verified high-resolution orbital imagery from NASA LROC and HiRISE. Virtual Reality is positioned as a zero-barrier, web-native tool rather than an isolated game: users can seamlessly transition from high-level planetary orbits to 1:1 ground-level inspection and back without installing external apps or plugins.

What factors did your team consider?

Universal accessibility (ensuring full functionality on budget smartphones without VR), strict historical and physical fidelity (Apollo DSKY 1240/960 Hz audio beeps, authentic gravitational constants, crash vs. soft landing classifications), and complete bilingual (English and Turkish) localization.
